sections.title: Cloud Service & Deployment Models
sections.content:
Service models — who manages what:
IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service) — provider gives VMs, storage, networking; you manage OS and up. (AWS EC2, Azure VMs.)
PaaS (Platform as a Service) — provider manages OS/runtime; you deploy just your app/code.
SaaS (Software as a Service) — provider runs the whole app; you just use it. (Microsoft 365, Salesforce.)
Mnemonic: the higher you go (IaaS -> PaaS -> SaaS), the LESS you manage.
Deployment models:
Public — shared provider infrastructure, multi-tenant.
Private — dedicated to one organization.
Hybrid — mix of public and private, connected.
Community — shared by organizations with common needs.
Shared responsibility model: the provider secures the cloud (hardware, hypervisor); the customer secures what they put IN the cloud (data, configs, access). Misconfiguration is the customer's fault.
exam_tips: IaaS = most customer control/responsibility; SaaS = least.
In the shared responsibility model, cloud misconfigurations are the customer's responsibility.

sections.title: Cloud Connectivity & Networking
sections.content:
Getting to and within the cloud:
VPC (Virtual Private Cloud) — your isolated virtual network inside a public cloud, carved into subnets.
VPN — encrypted tunnel over the public internet to the cloud (cheap, variable performance).
Direct Connect / ExpressRoute — a private, dedicated circuit to the cloud provider (consistent, higher performance, more cost).
Network security group (NSG) / security group — cloud firewall rules applied to subnets or instances.
Cloud gateway — NAT gateway, internet gateway, or VPN gateway that controls traffic in/out of the VPC.
NFV (Network Functions Virtualization) — running routers, firewalls, and load balancers as software instances instead of dedicated hardware.
exam_tips: Direct Connect/ExpressRoute = private dedicated link (predictable); site-to-site VPN = encrypted over the internet (cheaper, variable).
A VPC is your logically isolated slice of the provider's network.

sections.title: Modern & Evolving Network Environments
sections.content:
SDN (Software-Defined Networking) — separates the control plane (decisions about where traffic goes) from the data plane (actually forwarding it). A central controller programs the switches, enabling automation and central policy.
SD-WAN — applies SDN to WAN links; intelligently steers traffic across MPLS, broadband, and LTE based on application and link quality. Great for connecting branch offices to cloud apps.
SASE (Secure Access Service Edge) — converges SD-WAN with cloud-delivered security (firewall, CASB, zero trust) into one service.
Infrastructure as Code (IaC) — defining and deploying network/infrastructure through version-controlled scripts/templates (Terraform, Ansible) instead of manual clicks — repeatable and auditable.
Zero trust — 'never trust, always verify': authenticate and authorize every request regardless of location, with least privilege and microsegmentation.
IPv6 adoption, IoT, and cloud-first designs are the main drivers pushing these changes.
exam_tips: SDN splits the control plane from the data plane, with a central controller.
SD-WAN chooses the best path across multiple WAN transports per application.
Zero trust assumes breach: verify every request, enforce least privilege, segment heavily.

concept_cards.hook: Cloud service tiers by how much the provider manages: IaaS (VMs/networking), PaaS (runtime/platform), SaaS (full application). More abstraction = less you manage.
The provider secures the cloud infrastructure; the customer secures their data, configurations, and access within it.
Virtual Private Cloud — a logically isolated virtual network inside a public cloud, divided into your own subnets and security groups.
A private, dedicated physical circuit from your site to a cloud provider, giving consistent performance versus an internet VPN.
Software-Defined Networking — decouples the control plane from the data plane so a central controller can program forwarding behavior.
Software-defined WAN that dynamically steers traffic across multiple transports (MPLS, broadband, LTE) based on application needs and link health.
Provisioning and managing infrastructure through version-controlled definition files (Terraform, Ansible) rather than manual configuration.
A security model that trusts no user or device by default, verifying and least-privileging every request regardless of network location.

practice_questions.q: In which cloud service model does the customer manage the operating system and applications but not the physical hardware?
practice_questions.explanation: With IaaS the provider supplies infrastructure (VMs, storage, networking) and the customer manages the OS and up.

practice_questions.q: A retailer wants one service that combines SD-WAN with cloud-delivered firewall and zero-trust access. What is this?
practice_questions.explanation: SASE converges SD-WAN networking with cloud-delivered security (firewall, CASB, zero trust) into one service.

practice_questions.q: Under the cloud shared responsibility model, who is responsible for a misconfigured storage bucket exposing data?
practice_questions.explanation: Customers are responsible for securing what they put in the cloud, including configurations and access.

practice_questions.q: Which practice deploys network infrastructure from version-controlled templates for repeatable, auditable builds?
practice_questions.explanation: IaC defines infrastructure in version-controlled files (Terraform/Ansible) so deployments are repeatable and reviewable.

practice_questions.q: Which connection gives a private, dedicated, predictable-performance link to a cloud provider?
practice_questions.explanation: Direct Connect/ExpressRoute is a dedicated private circuit; an internet VPN is cheaper but variable.

practice_questions.q: Which technology separates the network control plane from the data plane using a central controller?
practice_questions.explanation: Software-Defined Networking (SDN) decouples the control plane from the data plane with a central controller.

practice_questions.q: A company runs its own virtual network, subnets, and security groups inside a public cloud. What is this called?
practice_questions.explanation: A VPC is a logically isolated virtual network within a public cloud provider.

practice_questions.q: Which approach dynamically steers branch traffic across MPLS, broadband, and LTE based on application needs?
practice_questions.explanation: SD-WAN selects the best transport per application across multiple WAN links.

practice_questions.q: Provisioning network infrastructure from version-controlled templates instead of manual configuration is called what?
practice_questions.explanation: Infrastructure as Code defines and deploys infrastructure through version-controlled files (Terraform, Ansible).
